What is motivational office wall art?

Motivational office wall art refers to art prints, canvas prints or framed artwork displayed in a workspace — home office, studio or commercial office — chosen specifically to inspire, energise or focus the person working there. Unlike purely decorative pieces, motivational office wall art is selected with intention: it might feature uplifting travel scenes that remind you of your goals, beautifully illustrated city prints that spark a sense of possibility, or calming imagery that keeps you grounded through a busy day. The right piece can genuinely shift the mood of a workspace, making it feel more personal, more creative and far more pleasant to spend time in. At AboutWallArt, our travel-style art prints — like this Paris autumn set — are a popular choice because they combine visual beauty with that quiet, daily reminder that life is full of wonderful things worth working towards.

How to Hang Motivational Office Wall Art as a Set of 3

1. Measure your wall space first: Hold a tape measure across the wall area you have in mind and note the width. For a set of 3 prints hung in a row, aim for a total span (including gaps) that sits comfortably within that space — roughly two-thirds of the wall width tends to look balanced rather than cramped or lost.

2. Mark your centre point: Find the horizontal centre of your wall section and mark it lightly with a pencil. Hang the middle print (the Eiffel Tower rooftop scene) centred on that point at eye level — approximately 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print is a good general rule for a seated workspace.

3. Space the flanking prints evenly: Position the left print (Montmartre café) and right print (Gothic cathedral) with an even gap of around 4–6 cm on each side of the centre piece. Use a spirit level — even a free phone app works — to keep all three perfectly aligned horizontally.

4. Choose your fixing method: Framed and canvas-wrapped options come ready to hang. For framed prints, use two wall hooks per frame for extra stability. For unframed prints, use a frame or poster hanger you love — this set suits simple slim natural wood or matt black frames beautifully.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, stand back at desk distance (roughly 1.5–2 metres) and check the spacing looks even. Tiny adjustments make a big difference — take your time and enjoy the process!

What is fireplace wall art?

Fireplace wall art refers to art prints or canvases chosen specifically to hang above a mantelpiece or chimney breast, acting as a focal point for the whole room. Because the fireplace is already a natural centre of attention, the art placed above it tends to carry more visual weight than pieces hung elsewhere, so size, colour, and composition all matter a great deal. A set of prints — like a coordinated trio of travel scenes — works especially well in this spot because the grouped arrangement has the scale to hold its own above the mantel without requiring a single oversized piece. How to Hang Art Prints Above a Fireplace — a Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Measure your chimney breast: Note the full width of the wall space above your fireplace. Aim for your grouped prints to span around two-thirds to three-quarters of that width so they feel proportional — not cramped and not swamped by the wall.

2. Find the right height: The bottom edge of your artwork should sit roughly 15 to 20 cm above the mantel shelf. Any lower and the art risks heat or soot damage over time; any higher and it starts to feel disconnected from the fireplace below.

3. Mark your spacing: For a set of three prints, use a pencil and a spirit level to mark out the centre point of your wall, then work outward with equal gaps of 5 to 8 cm between each print. Cut paper templates to the exact print size and stick them temporarily to the wall with masking tape — this lets you step back and check the arrangement before you commit to any hooks.

4. Hang level: Use a spirit level across all three hooks or picture rails before hanging. Even a slight tilt will be very obvious on a fireplace wall because the horizontal line of the mantel acts as a natural reference point.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three prints are up, step back to the opposite side of the room. Check that the grouping feels centred above the mantel and balanced in relation to any objects on the shelf below. Small adjustments now save a lot of fiddling later.

Unframed Print, Framed Print or Wrapped Canvas — Which Is Right for You?

aiItems.content:
What is house wall art?

House wall art refers to decorative prints, canvases or framed artwork designed to be hung on the walls of your home, adding personality, colour and style to any room. It covers everything from travel-inspired watercolour art prints to botanical illustrations, abstract designs and typographic pieces. Good house wall art does more than fill an empty wall — it sets the mood of a room, sparks conversation and reflects the personality of the people who live there. Available as unframed prints, framed prints or wrapped canvases, house wall art can be tailored to suit any interior style, colour scheme or budget.

How to Hang a Set of 3 House Wall Art Prints

1. Measure your wall space first: Use a tape measure to find the total width of wall you have available. For a set of 3 prints, aim for the combined width of all three to fill around two-thirds of the wall — this creates a balanced, intentional look rather than prints that feel lost or crowded.

2. Find your centre point: Mark the centre of your wall lightly with a pencil. Hang the middle print first, centred on this mark at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print). This anchors the arrangement.

3. Space the prints evenly: Hang the left and right prints with an equal gap between each one — 3 to 5 cm works well for most sets. Use a spirit level or a laser level to keep all three perfectly aligned horizontally.

4. Step back and check: Before making any final holes, hold the prints up with painter's tape or use paper templates cut to size. Step back across the room to check the spacing and height feel right from a distance — this is the view you'll have most often.

5. Choose your fixing method: For framed prints, standard picture hooks or adhesive strips work well on most walls. For wrapped canvases, a single D-ring hook per canvas is usually sufficient. Always check your wall type before fixing.

Choosing Your House Wall Art Print Format — What's the Difference?

Format — Unframed Print: The print only, ready for you to frame yourself or display as-is. Available in Luster art paper (slight sheen, vivid colour) or Museum quality paper (matte, gallery finish). Great if you already have a frame or want to choose your own.

Format — Framed Print: Your chosen art print comes ready mounted and framed — simply hang it straight on the wall. No need to source a frame separately. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper, in multiple sizes.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, with the image wrapping around the edges. Arrives ready to hang with no frame needed. Gives a contemporary, gallery-style finish. Available in multiple sizes.

Paper finish — Luster: A semi-gloss surface that brings out colour depth and fine detail — ideal if you want the watercolour tones in these Paris prints to really sing.

Paper finish — Museum quality: A smooth matte surface with a premium gallery feel — beautiful if you prefer a softer, more understated presentation with no surface reflection.

For more kitchen wall art inspiration and ideas on how to group prints together, take a look at our kitchen wall art collection — there are plenty of styles to mix and match if you fancy building out the look.

Choosing the Right Size and Style for Your Space

If your kitchen wall has a fair bit of room — say, above a long run of units or a dining table — I'd go for the larger size options so the set really holds its own and doesn't get lost. For a smaller wall or a tighter galley kitchen, a medium size works a treat and keeps things proportionate. The soft beige and grey backgrounds mean you genuinely don't need to worry too much about wall colour — these prints are forgiving and versatile.

In terms of finish, Luster art paper gives a gentle sheen that brings out the warm orange tones beautifully in natural light. Museum quality paper has a slightly more matte, gallery-like feel — lovely if your kitchen gets a lot of bright daylight. If you want something with a bit more texture and depth, the wrapped canvas option gives the whole set a really lovely tactile quality.

Scroll down to see how each size looks in a kitchen before you decide — there's a size-guide image below showing every option in situ so you can get a proper sense of scale.

aiItems.content:
What are kitchen prints for wall?

Kitchen prints for wall are decorative art prints chosen specifically to suit a kitchen or dining space — bringing colour, personality and a sense of style to what is often the busiest room in the home. They come in a wide range of subjects, from food and botanicals to travel and cityscape scenes like this autumn Paris set, and are available unframed, framed, or on wrapped canvas to suit different tastes and budgets. Unlike standard posters, quality kitchen wall art prints are produced with fade-resistant inks on art-grade paper or canvas so they hold their colour even in a room with fluctuating temperature and natural light. A set of three prints, like this one, is a popular choice because it creates an instant, curated look without the guesswork of mixing and matching individual pieces.

How to Hang Kitchen Prints for Wall: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Find a wall with enough clear space for all three prints side by side — above a counter, a dining table, or on a feature wall works well. Measure the total width available and divide by three to get an idea of the maximum print width per piece, leaving around 4–6 cm between each one.

2. Pick your size and format: Use the size guide image on this page to see how small, medium and large sizes look in a real kitchen. If the wall is wide, go larger; for a narrow or galley kitchen, a medium size is usually ideal. Decide whether you'd prefer unframed prints, framed prints (which arrive ready to hang), or wrapped canvas.

3. Mark your hanging points: Cut three pieces of paper the same size as your chosen prints and tape them to the wall with painter's tape to visualise the layout before you put any nails in. Adjust spacing until it looks balanced, then mark the top-centre of each with a light pencil dot.

4. Hang at eye level: As a general rule, the centre of each print should sit at roughly eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor. If you're hanging above a piece of furniture, aim for the bottom of the prints to sit about 15–20 cm above the top of the furniture.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back to check alignment. A small spirit level is your best friend here for making sure they're all perfectly straight. Then enjoy your new Parisian kitchen gallery!

Which Format Is Right for You? Comparing Your Options

Unframed Print — The print is shipped rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself or display in an existing frame. Available in Luster art paper (gentle sheen, warm tones) or Museum quality paper (matte, gallery feel). Great if you already have frames or want to choose your own.

Framed Print — Arrives completely ready to hang — no separate frame needed, no extra cost or hassle. Printed on Luster or Museum quality art paper and mounted inside the frame. Ideal if you want a polished, finished look straight out of the box.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, giving a tactile, textured finish with depth. No glass, no frame required — just hang and enjoy. A brilliant choice if you prefer a more relaxed, contemporary feel or want something that works without a border.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss surface that brings out warm orange and amber tones beautifully, with a gentle sheen. Works particularly well in kitchens with natural daylight.

Museum Quality Paper — A fine-art matte finish with excellent colour depth and a premium feel. Ideal for brighter kitchens or anyone who prefers a non-reflective surface.

Choosing the Right Size and Format for Your Wall

aiItems.content:
What is large artwork for living room?

Large artwork for living room refers to wall art prints or canvases sized to make a real visual impact in a lounge or sitting room — typically used as a focal point above a sofa, fireplace, or sideboard. Unlike small decorative prints, large artwork anchors the room and draws the eye, giving the space a finished, intentional feel. A set of three prints displayed together counts as large artwork because the combined visual weight fills a significant section of the wall. Choosing the right scale, colour palette, and subject for your living room is the key to making large wall art feel considered rather than overwhelming.

How to Hang Large Artwork for Living Room Walls

1. Measure your wall space first: Use a tape measure to find the width of the wall or the furniture piece below (such as a sofa). Aim for your artwork to span roughly two-thirds of that width for balanced proportions — this is the single most useful rule for getting scale right.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the horizontal midpoint of your wall or sofa and use a pencil mark or low-tack tape to plan where the centre print will sit. Hanging art so its centre sits at roughly 145–150 cm from the floor puts it at average eye level — a good starting point for most living rooms.

3. Plan your spacing for a set of 3: For a set of three prints, lay them out on the floor first to visualise the arrangement. A gap of 5–8 cm between each print looks neat and keeps the set reading as one cohesive piece rather than three separate pictures.

4. Use the right fixings: For larger or heavier framed prints, use wall plugs and picture hooks rated for the weight. For lighter unframed or canvas prints, picture strips or a single hook per print often does the job cleanly.

5. Step back and adjust: Once the first print is up, stand back at the distance you'd normally view it from before fixing the others — it's much easier to shift a pencil mark than to fill a nail hole.

Which Format Is Right for Your Living Room?

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself. Ideal if you have a specific frame style or colour in mind, or if you already own frames. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight away — no sourcing frames, no fuss. A great choice if you want a polished, gallery-style look with minimal effort. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper, in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed on canvas with the image wrapping around the edges of a deep wooden stretcher frame. No glass, no mount — just a clean, contemporary look that goes straight on the wall. A brilliant option if you prefer a more relaxed, tactile finish. Available in multiple size options.

Luster Art Paper — A subtle semi-sheen finish that reduces glare while keeping colours vivid. A versatile everyday choice that works well in most living rooms.

Museum Quality Paper — A premium fine-art paper that brings out the maximum depth and detail in the watercolour tones of this Paris set. Ideal if you want the closest thing to an original painting look.
